instruction: Procedural Material Library and Rule-Based Application The file `C:\Users\user\Desktop\materials.json` defines a small material library with 5 entries. The file `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rooms.dae` contains 5 separate named geometries representing different parts of a room, each named with a `Group<Part>_<MaterialKey>` suffix convention, for example `GroupFloor_Oak` is the floor mesh that should receive the `Oak` material. Materials (read exactly from `C:\Users\user\Desktop\materials.json`): - `Oak`: diffuse texture `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/oak.png`, UV scale 0.5 m (one tile spans 0.5 m in world space), lambert (matte wood). - `Marble`: diffuse texture `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/marble.png`, UV scale 2.0 m (one tile spans 2 m), lambert. - `Brass`: diffuse texture `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/brass.png`, tint colour `#b5a04a`, phong, shininess 80, glossy. - `Glass_50`: diffuse texture `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/glass.png`, tint colour `#eef6ff`, phong, transparency 0.5 (alpha half). - `Concrete`: diffuse texture `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/concrete.png`, tint colour `#a2a2a2`, lambert, matte (no shininess). 1. Parse `C:\Users\user\Desktop\materials.json`. 2. For each `<geometry>` in `C:\Users\user\Desktop\rooms.dae`, read its name and extract the material key from the `_<Key>` suffix (e.g. the `Oak` in `GroupFloor_Oak`). 3. Apply the material defined in `C:\Users\user\Desktop\materials.json` to that geometry, producing a COLLADA effect with the correct shading type, diffuse texture reference, and - where applicable - transparency, shininess, and tint colour. UV coordinates on each geometry must scale so that one texture tile spans exactly the declared UV-scale metres in world space. 4. Export `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`, bundling the referenced textures in a `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/` subdirectory (relative paths, e.g. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/oak.png`). Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` parses as valid COLLADA. 2. `<library_effects>` contains exactly 5 effects (one per material). 3. Each of the 5 geometries (`GroupFloor_Oak`, `GroupCountertop_Marble`, `GroupFaucet_Brass`, `GroupWindow_Glass_50`, `GroupWall_Concrete`) is present and bound via its scene node to the correctly-named material. 4. Each effect's diffuse input references the declared PNG file name, and that PNG exists on disk under `C:\Users\user\Desktop\tex/` next to `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. 5. The `Glass_50` effect has `<transparency>` = 0.5 within 0.01. 6. The `Brass` effect is phong with shininess >= 40. 7. UV coordinates on the Oak floor repeat at 0.5 m per tile (+/- 0.1) and on the Marble countertop at 2.0 m per tile (+/- 0.3). [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
